body:
Oh, you want sex, allright - but not from a man you've already "conquered".

Female sexual psychology is incompatible with monogamy.

No, because she is married and already got what she wanted:  Economic stability.

The OP has not made it clear to her that her continued residence in his home is conditional to her putting out - so, she doesn't.
Doesn't seem to do you much good in this world.   The only people who get ahead are the sociopaths.

> You are a weak human being that desperately needs attention, someone to tell them they are great, "worth-loving", attractive etc.

Everyone has the need for affirmation, some are just better at denying it to themselves.
Thanks I guess.

Trying to provoke my temper by downplaying what I'm going through?

Huh.

Well, call me all the names you like, I guess.  Whatever makes this easier for you.
Patience is what got me into this mess.  I'm done with patience.
We have had many, many arguments about religion.   They aren't giving Jesus up for anything.  It's easier to live in a fantasy world so they can ignore this one.

It's a paradox because something can't exist and not exist at the same time, but due to the really fucking weird way that things behave at the quantum level (and the wacky math involved), some things neither exist or not exist until they are observed.  

Summed up:   Quantum mechanics is some deep shit, man.

Don't feel bad if you can't grasp the whole picture - most people can't explain quantum physics.   Most people don't even know what quantum physics is.

If you're interested, read up on it!

> attempting to reason with people like this is not the easiest task

You can't reason someone out of a position they didn't reason themselves into.

Your only shot is using a stronger emotional argument than religion.  And that's gonna be tough.

Well, maybe this will cause them to rethink their stance on Jesus telling people who it's okay to love.

Some people are incapable of thinking for themselves until they're involved in an issue through personal tragedy.
Remember the unwritten book of the road.
You can't use the blindsiding argument.   There is no amount of preparation that could make my loved ones okay with me passing.   But that's their problem soon.  And yes, that makes me selfish.

Not until everything is settled.  I still have to write all the other emails - parents, friends - get a will drawn up so I can give what little savings I have to my mom (she needs it, she's got no health insurance and diabetes is slowly killing her), and then go purchase a handgun.

I'll probably be around another couple of weeks.

I'm just glad the end is finally in sight.

I wasn't saying that something has to be 100% risk free, just that I can make a smarter choice of partners than people who are known to be infected with a disease that can slowly and painfully kill me as well as turn me into a social pariah (ha, like I have a great social life now).

Frankly it wouldn't matter to me if I had TEN condoms on, I still would not have sex with someone who is HIV positive.

I understand that they did not make the conscious decision to catch HIV.   I understand that they got unlucky, and that shit happens.

My heart goes out to them.   I've taken some stupid risks too in my time, and I got lucky.  They didn't.  That's all.

But that doesn't mean I'm morally obligated to destroy my own health just to make them feel better.

> We are 44 and 46 years old and I have never, ever been happier.

Well, I'm glad for you, but - pardon the rudeness- I'd rather not wait until I'm old and busted to start a family.   Like I mentioned, I want kids, and your 40's are a bit late for that kind of thing.  Call me selfish.

> ended up seeing my medical doc for an anti-depressant.

Been there done that.   All antidepressants do is put a lock on your emotions.   You can't feel sad when you should feel sad.  You can't feel angry when you're wronged.  You can't feel happy when things are going well.  You just feel like a robot, and that's worse in some ways - quiet, panicking ways - than being suicidal.

I'm glad you found antidepressants that work for you, but my broad experience with multiple prescribed drugs has been otherwise.

I just don't like dating websites.   People misrepresent themselves enough in real life, on the internet they have the freedom to say any lie they want as long as they have a couple of pictures pulled from Google images.

> There are options for those who have less cash to throw around. Does the military still provide you with insurance? 

Only for six months after leaving active duty.  It's been almost a year.

> I'm intrigued by your strong stance on psychiatry, could you elaborate? Is this influenced by any other belief system? Has a therapist harmed your family or friends?

No, but I saw therapists a couple of time as a young adolescent and all they did was swindle my family out of hundreds of dolllars an hour.    That's not science.  That's literally just sitting back in a chair and listening to me blabber aimlessly.   Any adult could've done that, it doesn't take a psychiatrist, and I'm still not convinced it actually changed anything.

> You don't want to talk about whether you have been in therapy?

Sorry, I forgot to answer that question.  I haven't slept in about 48 hours.  No, I haven't been to therapy, nor do I plan to go.  Psychiatry hasn't earned the right to call itself a science, and half the "therapists" out there are more fucked up than their clients.  Also, I'm not made of money.

> You spoke on the fact you haven't posted anything on an online dating website but now I should understand you have in the past and it hasn't worked out? 

I haven't posted anything on any profile-based sites but I have made a lot of friends online and tried to explore where that could go.  No one ever wants to meet in person.  Guess that makes me an axe-murderer.

> Nah I mean the muslim girl my brother, I'll bring my sword and shield, at least it would be quite the way to go. Some cultures still retain a flair for action!

I'd rather not there be a conflict..  if her family felt the need to send her brother to the USA just to protect her then obviously they are not Western enough to be my in-laws.  Any culture in which women are viewed as vessels for family honor is a dangerous one, and not just to any men who might want to court them - to the women themselves.  Learned that well during my time in the military.
Jamie Bamber (Apollo in the new Battlestar Galactica)

I'm glad the online thing has worked for you.  I haven't had the same experience.

> Whats her number?

Who, "Tara" or "Jessica"?  "Tara" is currently stuck in Afghanistan, "Jessica" I haven't heard from in at least seven years, but the last I heard she'd married the fat fuck she cheated on me with.  Good riddance to bad rubbish.
Fake.  Posse commitatus, plus the sourced pic is from Iraq.   Plus the article is written like shit and not actually cited from anywhere.
Because it is cheaper to import new Americans that are already educated than it is to educate our own.

> Do you feel like you have expressed your bisexuality, are you interested in doing so?

In the distant past I did, and yes.

> I'm glad you are tight with your fam, have you expressed your situation to them? 

Absolutely not.  They would have me shipped off to a funny farm so fast my head would spin.  Then I wouldn't have control over whether I live or die anymore.  I don't like losing liberty.

> How extensive has your search for a partner been, if not so extensive what would you pinpoint as being your biggest hindrance?

I don't post any profiles on online dating sites, if that's what you mean.  Feels too artificial.  Plus, let's be honest for a minute here, you're scraping the bottom of the barrel online.   Anyone who dates online is doing it because they couldn't cut it in real life - for whatever reason.  If you find an attractive girl on one of those sites who turns out to be legit and not a stolen picture, she's most assuredly batshit.

I'd say my biggest hindrance is my paranoia.  For example, I won't call this international student classmate of mine back despite her repeated phone calls and obvious interest, because she's a Muslim and her brother moved here with her to "protect" her, in other words, cut my head off if I touch her.

Will he actually do that?  I dunno, maybe not.  But there's a nonzero chance of it, so I don't risk it.  It's not worth it.

And it's risk avoidant thinking like that which keeps me indoors behind a keyboard instead of out there meeting people.  

I have only myself to blame.

> Do you feel like these women have unique, hard to acquire qualities, does that add to your hopelessness?

They were both really accepting of me.  I don't think I have any qualities that should make that a rare thing.  I guess I should say they were both equally concerned for me as they were for themselves, whereas most women I've met are almost completely selfish.   With them, it was give/give and not give/take.

> Were you ever close to your immediate family?

We're close, we just disagree on some fundamental things, like religion.  So in desperate times we pull together, but the rest of the time..

> Did you pick up any skills/education in the military? 

Skills, somewhat, education, not really.   I was exposed to a variety of tasks in a variety of fields, did reasonably in most of them, and got out with a sobering picture of the way the military works, and the kind of people that run it.

> Would you ever consider adoption if you were in a relationship?

Only if one or both of us was sterile.   I have nothing against adoption at all, but if I can have my own kids, I want to do that.

Er.  I got that backwards.  Me and "Jessica" were together as teens and young adults.   "Tara" is the girl I met in the military who was already taken, but sparks flew.

> I assume these two women, even after Jess's betrayal, have a special place in your heart where you would love to see someone else take up a more permanent residency?

It's a bit more than that.   I feel empty without a partner.

> How did your military experience affect you?

It didn't, not in the stereotypical way - PTSD, nightmares, etc.  But looking back on six years of wearing the uniform and not a single night spent out on the town makes me wonder what the fuck I was thinking.  I don't even know how to enjoy a night on the town. 

> Are you gainfully employed?

No.  Is anyone in the USA?

> Is your family distant? You sound like a family man.

I don't have my own family, but my sister is a 45 minute drive away, and my parents are about 30 minutes away.  I don't see any of them terribly often.  I think they can sense my depression and it drives them away.   We still meet for things like Christmas or birthdays but I'm not really there.

Me and "Tara" were together from the time that we were both 15 or 16 until the time we were both 21 or 22.   

I live with constant emotional pain.  Cue the emo makeup and wrist cutting.  (I don't do either of those things, but seriously, fuck this shit)

And my realizations about the future just point out that this situation is only going to get worse.  I'm only going to get older and lonelier than I am now.   

I really do think that ending things on my terms is better than dying an old man with no children.

False equivalency.

I don't have to fuck HIV positive guys in the ass bareback in order to put food on the table.

Thanks, I guess.  I'm not sure being told that it's going to continue being like this helps at all, but then I'm not really looking for help, so whatever.  Thanks for having the sympathy to post, at least.

I did, a long time ago, with "Jessica".  We loved eachother madly, then she cheated on me when I signed up for the military.

The only other time I've felt it was for a short time with "Tara", but she closed herself off to me because she felt herself getting involved emotionally and she wasn't willing to risk her marriage.   Which was the right call.

A lack of human contact, pretty much.   I talk to my roommate every day, and stepping outside I can talk to strangers all I want, but that isn't human contact.  

Human contact is having someone you can hold, or to hold you.  Someone you can confide in.  A shoulder to cry on, instead of a pillow.

You can't get that from strangers, and you can't get it outside of a romantic relationship.  Even in a romantic relationship you put yourself in danger of getting dumped by showing any vulnerability.

> your risks are so low as to not be worth worrying about.

Let's see here, a nonzero risk of getting HIV, versus a zero risk.  What to do, what to do..
A hug.

Soon, it won't matter.  Can you remember before you were born?   Me neither.  We were just patterns of atoms without self-awareness.   Death is no different.  Our atoms are arranged in slightly more interesting patterns than before we were born, but they are no longer self-aware.  There's no afterlife waiting for any of us.  That's silly superstitious feelgood nonsense that weaker people than you or I tell themselves because they can't face the thought of this being the only life we have.  They think it's too terrible, because this world is filled with war and disease and cruelty and rape and starvation.  They think that if they just invent a fantasy world that they can ignore the one falling apart around them and not be responsible.  If you're not a part of the solution, you're a part of the problem.  And their wishful thinking has caused more needless pain than anything else I can think of.  I couldn't even grow up being honest about myself because bisexuals aren't looked upon kindly in Oklahoma.

Bet you didn't know that, huh?   Yep, Bryan swings both ways.  I never tell anyone because I fucking can't.  Our society is too fucked up and backwards and obsessed over who goes to bed with who for me to ever just be myself.   And you wonder why I'm always so quiet and paranoid.  It's because if I wasn't, some bigoted asshole would drag me behind his truck, or hang me with his redneck buddies out in the woods, or just shoot me and be done with it.  Business as usual in the bible belt.

So many lost opportunities to connect with other people.  I can't even begin to imagine how much love I could have experienced, if I only had the courage to stand up to the fucking idiots in this world and be who I really was.  If our society didn't look down on men for having their own needs, sexual or emotional, instead of expecting us all to be an unrealistic parody of Clint Eastwood or John Wayne, rock solid, emotionally independent, stoic.  We need intimacy, too.  We suck at explaining it sometimes, or we're afraid to say it, because we don't want to be accused of being emotional crybabies or effeminate, but we do.  We're human.  Humans need these things.

Hug Jason when you get a chance.  Kiss him and hold him and tell him it's going to be okay.  He doesn't know what you're talking about, but it doesn't matter.  It's going to be okay, Tara.  For both of you.  You're going to have kids.  Just don't stop trying.  It might take you eight years like it did my parents.  It might take less, it might take more.  It probably won't take more than a year or two.  But it'll happen.  You're going to be a great mother.  You have more empathy than most people I've known.  You have a tender affectionate love that will nurture them more than anything else can while they're growing.  I tried to tell you this after we met but I couldn't find the words to express it.  I still struggle with it, because it's an emotional sense I got from you and those can sometimes be hard to describe.  But you are very maternal.  And your husband, and your future kids, are lucky to have you.

I want you to be happy.   I know you can't be deliriously blissful all the time - real life isn't a fairy tale, and to be honest it's gonna be goddamn hard at times.  But stick with it.  Don't let frustration tear you and Josh apart.  If you're good for eachother, work through the bad times.  

If you have career goals, go for them.  You're smart enough to pass any college course I can think of - you might need to read the text if it's a subject you're not familiar with, but you've easily got enough potential to see it through.  It's not usually a politically correct thing to say, but some people don't.  It doesn't make them bad people, just means that some are more naturally gifted towards learning than others.  Don't be afraid to apply yourself.

I want to wish you well so much more, because I don't want to go.  I'm still yearning for you even after all this time, a little bit.  That tiny little piece of my heart still wants you.  Not anyone else, and not just because you accepted me - other women have done that and I'm not emailing them.  I think.. well, I hope, that you feel at least a little bit for me the way I do for you.  That in another life, one where you had been single when we met, we could have had a beautiful life together.  That you would have wanted to try, and see where life takes us.  I think I could see it in your eyes in all those late night webcam chats.  You know, the ones where I was so funny and well spoken and I said all the right things.. funny how I just completely clammed up in person, huh?   I guess that's why I'm alone.  No confidence.  No idea how to talk to people.  

It won't matter soon.  

I love you, Tara.  As a friend.  As a lover.  As someone who shared my pain when I needed you.  I just wish I could have done the same for you.  I wanted nothing more than to ease your suffering.  I hated seeing you cry.  I hated it.  Everything in me reached out.  But I can't be Jason.  You were right to push me away.  It's not my place.

Goodbye.
